# Patches to the vendored OpenSKP (third_party/openskp)

The subset is the parser only: the model, the VFF and MFC containers, the TLV and
page/dimension decoding, the transforms, and miniz. Six files are patched; each patch is a
standalone file in `patches/`, applied by `scripts/vendor-openskp.py`, and must apply cleanly
to the pinned commit.

## src/parser.cpp — drop the scene-builder wrappers

The patch file is `patches/parser.cpp.patch`.

Upstream's `parser.cpp` defines `SkpFile::build_scene`, `SkpFile::build_instanced_scene`,
`build_scene` and `build_instanced_scene`; their bodies call `build_scene_raw` and
`build_instanced_scene_raw`, which live in `scene.cpp` and `instanced_scene.cpp` - the scene
baker, which the subset excludes. A link that needed them would fail; nothing in the subset
calls them. The patch deletes the four definitions; the declarations in `parser.hpp` stay
(they are declared-but-undefined only if a caller asks for them, which the helper does not).

```diff
--- a/src/parser.cpp
+++ b/src/parser.cpp
@@ ... @@
-SkpFile SkpFile::build_scene(const ParseOptions& o) const { return openskp::build_scene(data_, o); }
-
-InstancedScene SkpFile::build_instanced_scene(const ParseOptions& o) const {
-  return openskp::build_instanced_scene(data_, o);
-}
-
 SkpModel parse_skp(ByteBuffer b, const ParseOptions& o) { return build_model(full_parse(b, o), o); }
-
-Scene build_scene(ByteBuffer b, const ParseOptions& o) {
-  return build_scene_raw(full_parse(b, o), o);
-}
-
-InstancedScene build_instanced_scene(ByteBuffer b, const ParseOptions& o) {
-  return build_instanced_scene_raw(full_parse(b, o), o);
-}
```

## src/internal.hpp — include the public headers it uses, not the umbrella

The patch file is `patches/internal.hpp.patch`.

Upstream's `internal.hpp` includes `openskp/openskp.hpp`, the umbrella that includes every
public header, exporters included; the exporters are the only headers that need tinygltf and
flatbuffers. The subset replaces the umbrella with the headers the sources actually use:

```diff
--- a/src/internal.hpp
+++ b/src/internal.hpp
@@ ... @@
-#include <openskp/openskp.hpp>
+#include <openskp/errors.hpp>
+#include <openskp/instanced_scene.hpp>
+#include <openskp/model.hpp>
+#include <openskp/observability.hpp>
+#include <openskp/parser.hpp>
+#include <openskp/scene.hpp>
```

The scene and instanced-scene headers are declarations only; their implementations are the
excluded `scene.cpp` and `instanced_scene.cpp`, so including the headers drags in nothing.
`export.hpp` (generated by CMake's `generate_export_header`, as upstream does) defines
`OPENSKP_EXPORT`; with `OPENSKP_STATIC_DEFINE` it is empty, as in upstream's static build.

The same patch file has a second hunk, which adds `RawDefinition::attribute_dicts`. It carries a
definition's dictionaries from the reader to `Definition` (see the three patches below):

```diff
@@ -79,6 +84,8 @@
   bool always_faces_camera{};
   bool shadows_face_sun{};
   bool is_image{};
+  // The definition's own attribute dictionaries (geometry.cpp, legacy.cpp), as Definition's.
+  ParsedAttrDictionaries attribute_dicts;
   GeometryBuilder builder;
 };
 
```

## include/openskp/model.hpp — a definition's attribute dictionaries

The patch file is `patches/model.hpp.patch`. ADR 0176's follow-up "attribute reporting" (2026-10-26)
needs the definition's own dictionaries (SketchUp's `ComponentDefinition` attributes), which the
pinned parser read for no file. `Definition` gains `attribute_dictionaries`, the same shape as
`Instance::attribute_dictionaries`. Nothing else in the public header changes.

```diff
--- a/model.hpp
+++ b/model.hpp
@@ -497,6 +497,10 @@
   bool shadows_face_sun{};
   /// Image entity flag.
   bool is_image{};
+  /// Every attribute dictionary attached to this definition, keyed by the dictionary's declared
+  /// name, with the values' native types (the same shape as Instance::attribute_dictionaries).
+  /// Empty when the file has none.
+  ParsedAttrDictionaries attribute_dictionaries;
 };
 
 /// Top-level model container holding all definitions, layers, materials, and styles.
```

## src/model.cpp — copy them into the public definition

The patch file is `patches/model.cpp.patch`. `definition()` moves the raw dictionaries into the
public `Definition`.

```diff
--- a/model.cpp
+++ b/model.cpp
@@ -120,6 +120,7 @@
   d.always_faces_camera = r.always_faces_camera;
   d.shadows_face_sun = r.shadows_face_sun;
   d.is_image = r.is_image;
+  d.attribute_dictionaries = std::move(r.attribute_dicts);
   for (auto& v : r.builder.vertices)
     d.vertices.emplace(v.first, Vertex{v.first, v.second[0], v.second[1], v.second[2]});
   for (auto& e : r.builder.edges) {
```

## src/geometry.cpp — read the VFF definition dictionaries

The patch file is `patches/geometry.cpp.patch`. In a VFF file a definition's own dictionaries sit in
its entity base (`8813`) under the `D007` container and the `DC05` payload, the same place the model's
own dictionaries sit (`collect_model_attribute_dictionaries`). `collect_definitions` reads them there
with the existing `extract_attribute_dictionaries`. The owner's file (SketchUp 2024) has four
definition dictionaries with 23 values, all in that place.

```diff
--- a/geometry.cpp
+++ b/geometry.cpp
@@ -443,6 +443,13 @@
           }
       }
       collect_geometry(e.children, d.builder);
+      // The definition's own attributes: its entity base's D007 container, read as the model's are.
+      for (auto& b : e.children)
+        if (b.tag == "8813")
+          for (auto& c : b.children)
+            if (c.tag == "D007")
+              for (auto& x : c.children)
+                if (x.tag == "DC05") extract_attribute_dictionaries(x.payload, d.attribute_dicts);
       if (auto id = entity_id(e)) out[*id] = std::move(d);
     }
     collect_definitions(e.children, out);
```

## src/legacy.cpp — read the legacy definition dictionaries

The patch file is `patches/legacy.cpp.patch`. The `CComponentDefinition` reader called `preamble()`
and discarded the attribute container it returns, as the instance reader keeps it. The definition
loop now extracts that container with the existing `extract_legacy_attribute_dictionaries`. The
fixture `attribute_reporting.skp` (written by OpenSKP's writer) carries a definition dictionary, and the
parser reads its four values.

```diff
--- a/legacy.cpp
+++ b/legacy.cpp
@@ -1027,7 +1027,7 @@
         r.raw(6);
       }
     } else if (n == "CComponentDefinition") {
-      preamble();
+      v->attrs = preamble();
       v->k = "definition";
       // undecoded base block: 13 bytes in SketchUp 3, 19 in 4, 20 from 5, 22
       // from 2017
@@ -1962,6 +1962,7 @@
         d.always_faces_camera = s.second.v->faces_camera;
         d.shadows_face_sun = s.second.v->shadows_face_sun;
         d.is_image = image_def_ids.count(s.first) != 0;
+        d.attribute_dicts = extract_legacy_attribute_dictionaries(s.second.v->attrs, ar.slots);
         fill(d.builder, s.second.v->ents, ar.slots);
         out.definitions[s.first] = std::move(d);
       }
```

## Moving the pin

Re-run `scripts/vendor-openskp.py update <dir>` from the new commit archives; re-prove the
subset compiles and `parse_skp` links, and re-run the corpus before moving.
